goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher thinks aloud through a search plan for the hook case (key words drawn from a short background paragraph, synonyms, an exact phrase in quotation marks, which kind of source to try first) and turns one finding into a chain of new questions

note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: fix one poor query (g5-search-revise) and sort four questions, rewriting one (g5-research-or-guess), both last used in library grade 5 unit 1. Candidate kept: the continuum's several note forms, as a choice of two card layouts (no minutes added). Honest use without shaming (Sensitive ground, item 4): the copied practice sentence is invented; a student's own copied sentence is fixed with them privately. goal: Show-me: the hook (two invented pages on one claim, one polished and wrong, one plain and right) and the compelling question, then the teacher thinks aloud through lateral reading: leave the page, see what others say about its maker and claim, go upstream to the original, and judge whether it is accurate, fair in context and fit for the task
note: Skill card "leave the page, ask who is behind it, go upstream, then judge", held by the teacher. It grows grade 5's "what others say" card by "go upstream", and it maps to the grades 9 to 12 routine card, the band's end form (stop, investigate the source, look for better coverage, trace the claim): leave the page is stop, ask who is behind it is investigate the source, seeing what others say about the maker and claim is look for better coverage, go upstream is trace the claim; then judge is the verdict those steps lead to. The method, not a checklist of looks: the polished page fails and the plain one passes. Exit ticket: one claim checked on a "what others say" card. Cases invented, no partisan question, a hoax page described or invented, never reproduced (Sensitive ground, item 1). Leans on the CC BY online-reasoning lessons, not yet in the source store (later.csv L149): planned from the frame; when loaded, the item license is re-read at source and its credit goes on the day (intro lessons; lateral versus vertical reading). Supplies: printed invented pages and "what others say" cards; one projector optional

goal: Show-me: the point of view a source takes (word choice, what is left out, who paid for it), weighed in an "I trust this less because..." or "This fits because..." line; then pairs practice yesterday's move, three claims checked laterally on "what others say" cards
note: Opens with unit 1's respond step: each student fixes the sitting item the error letters marked (5 minutes), then the five-minute retrieval task: one unfamiliar page checked by leaving it (g5-first-lateral-check) and one line on where three short sources agree and differ (g5-evidence-notes), both library grade 5. A class that did not take library grade 5 gets the ten-minute reteach from that grade 5 unit's show-me case for every student, in place of the five-minute task. Candidate kept: the continuum's grade 6 cell on inaccurate or misleading information, at the upstream step: one of the three claims is misleading because its quote was cut (no minutes added). Leans on the CC BY online-reasoning lessons, not yet in the source store (later.csv L149): planned from the frame; when loaded, the item license is re-read at source and its credit goes on the day (lateral reading with an encyclopedia site).
